group:paper-mock-jiangsu-wuxi-2026-01-se.overview: 本文谈怎样面对自己犯下的错误：在承担责任的同时接纳情绪，能补救就补救，不沉溺于懊悔，再从大局客观看待错误，把错误变成反思和成长的机会。
group:paper-mock-jiangsu-wuxi-2026-01-se.fullTranslationZh:
无论是伤害了别人的感情，还是把工作项目搞砸了，我们都可以把错误当作停下来、反思并重新振作的机会。毕竟，定义我们的不是我们犯的错误，而是我们对待错误的方式。
在承担责任的同时接纳情绪。这意味着要为自己的所作所为负责。与此同时，不要责怪自己，也不要因为那些“本应该”而折磨自己。另外，让自己去感受所有的情绪，无论是一点点尴尬，还是深深的懊悔。
如果可以，就去弥补。有时仅仅意识到错误还不够——它需要你作出回应。记住，真诚地去尝试永远不会太晚。目的不在于“把事情做对”，而只是减轻我们造成的伤痛，并尽己所能解决眼前的问题。
不要困在自己的错误里。鉴于人脑天生倾向于关注负面情绪，要走出懊悔需要下定决心。当你发现自己的思绪又飘向那种糟糕的感受、飘向自己为什么没做得更好时，停一下，深吸一口气。之后，把注意力转到真正值得关注的事情上。
着眼大局。有时，我们眼中的错误，恰恰是改变一段关系所必需的突破。又或许，从长远来看，让我们感到尴尬的事其实算不了什么。通过客观地看待事情，我们也许会发现，所谓的错误并没有我们起初以为的那么可怕的影响。

selectedLongSentences.sourceText: Given the fact that the human brain is naturally programmed to focus on negative emotions, it takes commitment to walk away from our regrets.
selectedLongSentences.displayText: Given the fact that the human brain is naturally programmed to focus on negative emotions, it takes commitment to walk away from our regrets.
selectedLongSentences.translationZh: 鉴于人脑天生倾向于关注负面情绪，要走出懊悔需要下定决心。
selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主干是 it takes commitment to walk away from our regrets：it 是形式主语，真正的主语是后面的不定式 to walk away from our regrets，“it takes + 名词 + to do”表示“做某事需要……”。句首 Given the fact that … 作状语，given 在这里相当于介词，意为“考虑到”；that 引导同位语从句，说明 the fact 的内容，从句中 is programmed to focus on 是被动结构，意为“天生被设定成关注”。这句交代走出懊悔为什么难，为本段后面“停下、深呼吸、转移注意力”的具体做法作铺垫。

underlineRanges.quote: to walk away from our regrets

selectedLongSentences.sourceText: By looking at things objectively, we might see that our so-called mistake doesn’t have the terrible impact we initially thought it did.
selectedLongSentences.displayText: By looking at things objectively, we might see that our so-called mistake doesn’t have the terrible impact we initially thought it did.
selectedLongSentences.translationZh: 通过客观地看待事情，我们也许会发现，所谓的错误并没有我们起初以为的那么可怕的影响。
selectedLongSentences.analysisZh: 主干是 we might see that …，that 引导宾语从句作 see 的宾语。句首 By looking at things objectively 是介词 by 加动名词，表示方式。宾语从句的主干是 our so-called mistake doesn’t have the terrible impact；后面的 we initially thought it did 是省略了关系词的定语从句，修饰 impact，其中 did 代替 had，整个从句意为“我们起初以为它会造成的（影响）”。这句把空前“错误也许并不严重”的说法落到“客观看待”的做法上。

discourseStructure.summary: 首段提出观点：错误可以成为反思和振作的机会，关键在于怎样应对；后四段各以一句祈使句开头，依次给出四条做法：负责并接纳情绪、尽力补救、别困在懊悔里、着眼大局。

units.summary: 以伤人感情、搞砸工作为例，提出错误可以成为停下、反思、振作的机会，重要的是怎样应对。
四条做法：承担责任又接纳情绪；能补救就补救，不求完美；察觉懊悔时停下深呼吸，转移注意力；放长远、客观地看待错误。

B.text: 选项借了第 37 题空后的尴尬和懊悔（embarrassment、regret），又像其他段首句一样是祈使句。但空后明说 "let yourself feel all your emotions"，与 "Avoid feeling" 正相反。放进第 39 题也接不上：空前 "take a deep breath" 后要给注意力找去处，它只说回避感受。
quotes: let yourself feel all your emotions

C.text: 选项的 "figure out why" 像在接第 36 题空前的 "reflect"，"mistake" 也是全文话题词。但后文讲负责、补救、放下、看大局，没有一段分析犯错原因，第 39 题所在段还劝人别老想 "why you didn’t do better"。放进第 38 题也接不上：空前 "awareness itself isn’t enough" 已说光认识不够，它又退回去找原因。

completedSourceTexts.text: Whether we’ve hurt someone’s feelings, or messed up a work project, we can use our errors as opportunities to stop, reflect, and bounce back. After all, what defines us isn’t our mistakes but the way we react to them.

Accept emotions while taking responsibility. This means taking responsibility for what you did. At the same time, don’t blame yourself or beat yourself up over the “shoulds”. Also, let yourself feel all your emotions, whether it’s a little embarrassment or a lot of regret.

If you can, fix it. Sometimes awareness itself isn’t enough – it calls for a response. Remember, it’s never too late to make a genuine attempt. The purpose isn’t to “get it right,” but to simply ease whatever pain we’ve caused and do whatever is in our power to resolve the matter at hand.

Don’t get stuck in your mistakes. Given the fact that the human brain is naturally programmed to focus on negative emotions, it takes commitment to walk away from our regrets. When you find your thoughts wandering to how awful it feels and why you didn’t do better, stop for a moment and take a deep breath. After that, redirect your attention to something that truly deserves it.

Look at the big picture. Sometimes what we perceive as a mistake is the breakthrough that was necessary to change a relationship. Or maybe what we feel embarrassed about isn’t a big deal in the long run. By looking at things objectively, we might see that our so-called mistake doesn’t have the terrible impact we initially thought it did.
